A: Fix metal materials: scope tube, rings, ocular housing and bolt body read as polished chrome. Make the scope matte/satin black hard-anodized aluminium (roughness ~0.45-0.6, broad soft highlights) and the bolt dull nitrided/blued steel (dark grey, roughness ~0.35-0.5) with a slightly brighter polished bolt-raceway wear band only

Build real optics: lenses need glass with layered anti-reflective coatings (faint green/magenta/amber reflections), visible internal lens elements and tube depth, and a reticle/exit pupil visible in the eyepiece view; the ADS view must not be a black void

Chassis finish: replace the flat procedural grain with a believable cerakote/anodize response (subtle sheen variation, micro-roughness breakup), and add edge wear on corners, screw heads, mag well lip, bolt handle path, plus light dust/fingerprints/handling smudges

Consistent machined chamfers on all chassis, stock and rail edges (1-2 mm with crisp catch-lights); remove knife-sharp edges and visible polygon facets on round parts (eyecup, bells, rings, bipod feet) by raising segment counts
Add markings: serial/caliber stamping on the action, turret numerals and hash marks, scope magnification ring numbers, rail slot numbers, small generic maker-style logo; empty surfaces scream CG
Rework the pistol grip and buttpad: proper rubber overmold texture/stippling, realistic finger contour, ribbed rubber recoil pad; stock spacers and cheek riser need hardware and real thickness detail
Small-part scale and detail: thinner screw heads with hex sockets, finer and denser turret knurling, deeper picatinny slots, a magazine with visible top cartridge/follower and a release latch

Photographic presentation: put the rifle on a surface (table, mat, ground) with contact shadows and bounce light, use a key/fill/rim photo setup with a softbox reflection on the metal, shallow depth of field and slight lens vignetting/grain for close-ups; the bipod must rest on a ground when deployed
Colour: chassis reads as light primer grey-green; push towards a real OD/FDE/black cerakote value and saturation with slight hue variation
B: Fix the scope tube material everywhere (FP shot shows it chrome): black hard-anodized aluminium, base colour ~sRGB 18-24 (linear ~0.006-0.009), metallic 0 to 0.2 (anodize behaves dielectric-ish) or metallic 1 with very dark albedo, roughness 0.35-0.5 with low-frequency roughness variation +-0.05, and a fine circumferential lathe/brush anisotropy. Check the FP shot uses the same material/LOD as the hero.

Build a real ADS view: render-target or textured reticle (e.g. mil-dot/Christmas-tree style, generic) on the ocular, an image of the scene through the scope with circular exit pupil and soft dark vignette ring, faint chromatic fringe at the edge. A black disk is unacceptable for a sniper.

Chassis material: replace the single-value grey-green with a Cerakote/anodize stack: base colour variation +-3% value via large-scale noise, orange-peel micro normal (0.2-0.5 mm scale, intensity low), roughness 0.55-0.7 base with polished/worn areas down to 0.35-0.45 on handled zones; add edge wear exposing bare aluminium (light grey, metallic 1, roughness 0.3-0.4) on forend tip edges, stock toe, cheek riser corners, mag well lips and bolt-side of the receiver; add dust/grime in recesses (AO-driven, slightly lighter and rougher).

Bevels: add 0.6-1.2 mm chamfers on every chassis and stock edge, 0.3-0.5 mm on small parts (screws, rings, turrets), with weighted normals so the highlight line reads; chamfer the inner walls of the M-LOK slots and let the barrel show through them.

Bolt: matte/satin finish (nitrided black or bead-blasted steel, roughness 0.3-0.5, not mirror); add the bolt's helical/jewelled or fluted body pattern, extractor and handle root transition; bolt knob tapered with cut knurling (diamond pattern ~1 mm pitch as real geometry normal map), not a perfect sphere.

Raise segment counts on all round parts seen close (eyepiece, objective bell, turrets, barrel muzzle, bipod tubes): minimum 48-64 sides on the scope bells and eyepiece, or smooth-shaded with proper normals so no facets show on silhouettes.

Objective/ocular glass: dark with thin multicoating tint (green/amber/magenta Fresnel, low saturation), IOR ~1.52, environment reflections; show internal lens element rings and a black baffled interior instead of a flat blue-purple disk.

Small-part detail: engrave turret numerals and hash ticks (0-10 with half-marks), a zero-stop line, Torx/hex recesses in ring cap and chassis screws, Picatinny slot crosscuts with chamfer, magazine feed lips and floorplate seam, pistol grip stipple texture and smoother sculpted contour.

Stock: break up the box forms of the butt and cheek riser with radiused transitions, a real rubber recoil pad (soft rubber, roughness 0.8-0.9, slight sheen, moulded texture), and adjustment wheels/levers with knurling.
Bipod: knurled leg-lock collars, visible springs and pivot hardware, matte rubber feet with tread and dirt; legs in hard-anodized black rather than plastic-looking smooth tubes.
Barrel: add slight muzzle carbon darkening and matte Cerakote finish (roughness 0.6), subtle heat discolouration near the muzzle device, and a crowned muzzle detail.

Presentation: render on a surface or HDRI with a contact shadow and real environment reflections (outdoor overcast HDRI suits anodize); the grey void with flat fill makes everything read as a turntable render.
